mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an ultra-accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 60-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5%, it indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.1% and the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0%, it signals an aggressive monetary policy response to a severe labor market downturn, which typically boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary policy response to labor market stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1 and UNRATE > 7.0, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1500 thousand units, it signals a contraction in the residential construction sector, which is a key component of aggregate demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1500, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (2017=100), it indicates a contraction in the manufacturing and industrial sector, which reduces corporate output and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) falls below 500,000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500 thousand units, it signals a severe contraction in the residential sector of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS < 500000 and HOUST < 1500, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL index exceeds 260 (1982-1984=100), it indicates persistent inflation that may trigger monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 260, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the number of persons employed in the private sector falls below 140,000 thousand, it indicates a severe labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 140000, or the rank correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
